profile.org_note: Fifteen markets, each an operating segment, roll up into two reportable segments (East, Central); management uses two named regional presidents (Texas: Lindsay Motley; Florida and Tennessee: Dan Fitzpatrick), while Atlanta, the Carolinas, Phoenix and Denver have no published regional president and appear to report to COO Ryan Lewis (inferred). Each division has its own land acquisition and development staff, but corporate (Alpharetta) gives final approval on every land acquisition and allocates capital; the corporate land head is SVP of Land Acquisition & Strategy Thad DiGiuro, and financing runs through CFO/CAO Zack Sawyer with VP and Corporate Controller Michael Escarra (no treasurer is named). The CEO, CFO and COO are the chief operating decision makers. Published investor contact: investor.relations@ashtonwoods.com.
profile.summary: Largest private US homebuilder by closings (10,080 homes closed in the fiscal year ended May 31, 2026; average price $355,000), building in 15 Sunbelt and Southeast markets across 8 states under Ashton Woods Homes (design-led move-up) and Starlight Homes (entry-level; 57% of orders in the quarter ended August 31, 2026 per HousingWire). It is already very land-light: 54,317 lots controlled at August 31, 2026, of which only 12.2% (6,650) were owned and 87.8% (47,667) were under purchase and option contracts, with about a 5.5-year supply at fiscal year-end. Privately held (99% by Little Shots Nevada L.L.C., family trusts linked to Great Gulf Group) but reports like a public company because of its senior notes, and entered Denver in 2025 as its newest market.
